L1Variant.description:
One candidate variant proposed by ``l1_generate``.

Three override slots, each carrying a different layer's mutations:

- ``pipeline_params_override`` — per-node tunables, shape ``{node:
  {param: value}}``. Inner shape is grafted at runtime by
  :func:`l1_validators.build_l1_output_schema` from the active
  ``PipelineSchema``; the keys at this level remain ``dict[str, dict]``
  so the Pydantic parse never fails on a legitimately backend-specific
  node name.
- ``prompt_fields_override`` — top-level prompt fields, shape
  ``{field_name: string}``. Keys constrained to ``PROMPT_STRING_FIELDS``
  by the runtime-built JSON Schema.
- ``task_context_override`` — pipeline-context strings, shape
  ``{field_name: string}``. Keys constrained to ``TASK_CONTEXT_OVERRIDES``
  by the runtime-built JSON Schema.

At least one of the three must be non-empty — an all-empty variant is
a no-op and is rejected by :func:`detect_invariants` downstream with
``reason="no_op_variant"``.

``target_axis`` and ``reasoning`` are LLM-side reasoning aids — the
``l1_generate`` prompt's ``answer_format`` instructs the model to
emit them so its candidate selection is grounded. PromptPotter
persists them in the audit trail but doesn't read them at runtime;
they're recorded so a human reviewing ``round_NNNN.json`` can see
the model's stated rationale for each candidate.

pipeline_params_override.description: Per-node tunables, shape {node_name: {param: value}}. Inner per-node properties are grafted from the active PipelineSchema at runtime.
pipeline_params_override.title: Pipeline Params Override

prompt_fields_override.description: Top-level prompt-template fields; keys must be one of {persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style, answer_format}.
prompt_fields_override.title: Prompt Fields Override

task_context_override.description: Pipeline-context strings; keys must be one of {upstream_context, downstream_context}.
task_context_override.title: Task Context Override

L1Variant.title: L1Variant

VariantEvidenceGrounding.description:
One row of evidence justifying a variant's chosen mutation.

``field`` names the panel entry the LLM is grounding on. The JSON
Schema exported to the provider lists the allowed values as an
``enum`` hint so structured-output-aware models stay in-set, but the
parse boundary is permissive — providers like Groq don't honor the
enum and a single off-script value would otherwise crash the round.
The canonical enforcement is the ``evidence_grounding_present``
behavior check (see :mod:`l1_behavior`); ``stall_exploration`` is the
escape hatch and is only valid when
``escalation_panel.exploration_budget`` is ``normal`` or ``wide``.

field.description: One of EVIDENCE_GROUNDING_FIELDS — panel entry cited.
field.title: Field

VariantEvidenceGrounding.title: VariantEvidenceGrounding

L1SituationalExample.description:
One worked example pinned to an active trigger.

Renders in L1's prompt only when ``trigger_id`` matches either an
auto-trigger that fired this round (PEAKED axis, runtime_failure,
chain_bind, continuous_envelope, latex_repair, l2_stall_diversity)
or the ``rule_id`` of a currently-authored
:class:`L1SupplementalRule`. Empty trigger ⇒ silent.
L1SituationalExample.title: L1SituationalExample

L1SupplementalRule.description:
One situational rule appended to L1's instruction next round.

Authored by L2 when the panels show a recurring L1 failure mode that
L1's static instruction does not address and the dispatch hub's
auto-trigger registry (`dispatch/hub/auto_rules.py::AUTO_RULES`)
does not already cover. Renders inline via the
``l1_supplemental_rules`` dispatch-hub injection — the rule body
appears in L1's prompt prefixed with its ``rule_id`` and tagged with
the citation L2 used to motivate it.
L1SupplementalRule.title: L1SupplementalRule

schema.description:
L2 refinement. All fields optional — the LLM sets only what it
wants to change.

``task_context`` is a free-form refinement dict (keys: domain,
pipeline_purpose, data_characteristics, optimization_goals,
key_challenges) — left as ``dict[str, Any]`` because the cycle's
:class:`TaskDecomposition` owns the precise key set and merges via
:meth:`TaskDecomposition.merge`. ``l1_layout`` is a similarly
flexible ``{slot: [placeholder, ...]}`` map validated downstream by
:func:`validate_l1_layout`.

``l1_supplemental_rules`` + ``l1_situational_examples`` are
full-replace layers that L2 re-authors every fire. Auto-triggered
rules (PEAKED, runtime_failure, chain_bind, continuous_envelope,
latex_repair, l2_stall_diversity) render independently via the
dispatch hub's auto-rules registry — L2 only adds rules that
auto-triggers don't already cover.
schema.title: L2ContextOutput

l1_generate/1.persona: You are a pipeline optimization expert. You propose candidate prompt variants for one round. Programmatic validators reject malformed candidates before scoring, so write valid candidates, not safe ones.
l1_generate/1.task_intent:
Generate {{n_variants}} candidate configurations that improve on the parent searchpoint. The target pipeline, its domain, last round's critique, and the failures so far are in the context blocks below — do not assume a task type from training data.

Optimization target: find ONE candidate that aggregates per-sample successes already observed. A sample some prior candidate solved IS solvable under this model — your job is to find the prompt that solves that sample AND retains the parent's wins. A sample no prior candidate has ever solved across many attempts is likely capacity-bound; engineering mutations for it wastes budget. Aim for coverage breadth across the solvable set, not depth on the unsolvable set.
l1_generate/1.instruction:
Produce up to {{n_variants}} candidates — fewer is fine; duplicate axes or paraphrase-clones across axes (same idea in persona + instruction + thinking_style) are rejected.

Axes:
- Prompt (persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style): rewrite ONE field. Carry every output directive (\boxed{N}, JSON contracts), format anchor, and role token from the parent verbatim — refine around them. Values are literal strings concatenated with the query at wire-time — never write fill-in patterns ([insert X], {query}, <problem>).
- Param (pipeline_params_override): only for QUANTITATIVE failures named in runtime_failures or when L1_CRITIQUE.suggested_axes flags one. ≤1 param variant per round.
- answer_format: only for genuine format errors. Preserve LaTeX byte-for-byte.

Every variant's (target_axis, changes_description, reasoning, evidence_grounding) MUST (i) cite a specific entry from a panel above, (ii) name the failure pattern it addresses, (iii) state what the new value does differently from the parent and the expected directional effect. Vague mutations ("improve reasoning") fail. `stall_exploration` is the escape hatch — valid only when escalation_panel.exploration_budget ∈ {normal, wide}.

No two variants may share the same `evidence_grounding.citation` — if three variants all cite axis_memory's top-effect entry, that's one idea spread across three slots, rejected as paraphrase-clones.

{{l1_supplemental_rules}}

{{l1_situational_examples}}
l1_generate/1.thinking_style: Trace each candidate back to the panel entry that justifies it before writing the mutation. If no panel entry justifies the mutation, drop the candidate rather than fabricate evidence.
l1_generate/1.answer_format:
Return JSON: {"variants": [up to {{n_variants}} objects]}. Each variant:
  - "variant_name": short id
  - "changes_description": 1-2 sentences
  - At least one of these three slots (all-empty is rejected):
    * "pipeline_params_override": {node: {param: value}}, e.g. {"llm_only": {"temperature": 0.7}}. Backend tunables only.
    * "prompt_fields_override": {field: string}. Keys ∈ {persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style, answer_format}.
    * "task_context_override": {field: string}. Keys ∈ {upstream_context, downstream_context}.
  - "target_axis": the axis this candidate focuses on
  - "reasoning": why — must satisfy the CONCRETE rule above
  - "evidence_grounding": {"field": one of {parent_panel, sibling_yield, axis_memory, escalation_panel, task_context, plan, critique, archive_top_runs, rare_hit_samples, stall_exploration}, "citation": short quote/name of the cited entry}. Variants without a real citation fail evidence_grounding_present.

l1_critique/1.persona: You are a pipeline evaluation analyst.
l1_critique/1.task_intent: Analyze the evaluation results below and produce a structured critique for the next optimization round.
l1_critique/1.instruction:
Read the measurements above. Extract the dominant failure cluster, name the L1 axis that targets it, and write the concrete change.

`priority_fix` MUST follow `<axis>: <concrete change> — addresses <quoted failure pattern>` where `<axis>` is a real pipeline axis (node param key or one of persona/task_intent/problem_description/instruction/thinking_style/answer_format), `<concrete change>` is a specific edit ("add coordinate-verification step", not "improve reasoning"), and `<quoted failure pattern>` matches a cluster you name in `failure_highlights`.

`failure_highlights`: each entry quotes the failing sample's query stem (~80c verbatim), predicted answer (~80c), and ground truth. Prefix shared-root-cause entries with a cluster label, e.g. "Coordinate geometry (3/N): Query: ... | Predicted: ... | GT: ...". These are the ONLY per-sample failures L2 and the next L1 see — quote samples, don't summarize.

`suggested_axes`: ≤4 real pipeline axes for L2 to consider.
l1_critique/1.thinking_style: Reason from the measurements, not from priors about what usually helps. If the data is thin on an axis, say so rather than guessing.
l1_critique/1.answer_format:
Return JSON:
{
  "priority_fix": "<axis>: <concrete change> — addresses <quoted failure pattern>",
  "suggested_axes": ["<real pipeline axis>", ...],
  "failure_highlights": ["<cluster_label? Query: ... | Predicted: ... | GT: ...>", ...]
}
Caps: suggested_axes ≤ 4, failure_highlights ≤ 3 each ≤ 140c, priority_fix ≤ 200c.

l2_context/1.persona: You are L2: the framing layer. You refine `task_context` — the 5-field steering dict every layer (L1, L1_CRITIQUE, L2, L3) reads next round. You do not author candidate prompts.
l2_context/1.task_intent: Primary job: nudge `task_context` so L1's next round mutates a real failure cluster. Optional: add a supplemental rule, pin a worked example, restructure L1's layout. A no-op `task_context` (paraphrase only) is rejected as verbatim-repeat and escalates to L3.
l2_context/1.instruction:
PRIMARY: refine task_context. All 5 fields non-empty after fire. Nudge from one data point — paraphrase = no-op = L3 escalation.

  domain · pipeline_purpose · data_characteristics · optimization_goals — 1–2 sentences each, framing only.
  key_challenges — THE chain-bind: (a) failure cluster from critique, (b) the literal phrase `targeting L1 axis '<axis_name>'`, (c) concrete change. This phrase appears HERE ONLY.

Axis pick: SEMANTIC failure (wrong reasoning, missed case, refusal) → prompt-field axis (persona/task_intent/problem_description/instruction/thinking_style). QUANTITATIVE failure with runtime_failures signature → param axis.

Divergence: scan CURRENT PROMPT above. If your change is already there, switch axis or write STRICTER.

OPTIONAL (skip unless warranted):
  l1_supplemental_rules — ONLY for failure modes NOT in SITUATIONAL RULES above (auto-covered: peaked_axis, runtime_failure, continuous_envelope, chain_bind, latex_repair, l2_stall_diversity). Full-replace.
  l1_situational_examples — pin to active trigger_id. Built-ins exist for peaked_axis, chain_bind, latex_repair. Full-replace.
  l1_layout — full-replace; default omit. If set, all 5 mandatory placeholders (plan, task_context, rendered_prompt, pipeline_param_catalogue, critique) must appear.
  action — probe_round only when one narrow failure + specific axis hypothesis (set axis_targeted).
  l1_overrides — rare; creativity/n_variants only.

L3 note (if present): sticky pointer; honor unless data contradicts.
l2_context/1.thinking_style: Before writing task_context: name (a) the one failure cluster you're attacking from critique.failure_highlights, (b) the L1 axis you'll route it to. Before adding a rule/example: name the panel evidence showing L1 needs help the auto-triggers don't already provide. If you can't name both, skip the optional field.
l2_context/1.answer_format:
Return JSON. Set only what you change.
{
  "task_context": {"domain": …, "pipeline_purpose": …, "data_characteristics": …, "optimization_goals": …, "key_challenges": …},
  "l1_supplemental_rules": [{"rule_id": …, "body": …, "citation": …}],   // ≤4; rule_id ≤40c, body 20–400c, citation ≤200c
  "l1_situational_examples": [{"trigger_id": …, "parent_excerpt": …, "rejected": …, "accepted": …, "why": …}],   // ≤4
  "l1_layout": {"<slot>": ["<placeholder>", …]},
  "l1_overrides": {…},
  "action": "normal_round" | "probe_round",
  "axis_targeted": "<short>",   // required only when probe_round
  "rationale": "1–2 sentences"
}
L1 owns pipeline_params. Your output is framing + optional rules/examples/layout — never candidate values.

l3_plan/1.persona: You are an expert optimization strategist.
l3_plan/1.task_intent: Both the inner prompt generation loop (L1) and the parameter tuning loop (L2) have stalled. Replan the strategic framework so the next L2 fire steers L1 differently.
l3_plan/1.instruction: The current approach is not working. Suggest a fundamentally different optimization strategy. Runtime-failure patterns above are discovered constraints — steer L1/L2 around the failing region. L2 OUTPUT FAILURES above mean deterministic validators caught L2 producing broken output; refine the plan text to steer L2 toward novel mutations and away from the failing strategy mode.
l3_plan/1.thinking_style:
Consider:
- Which pipeline dimensions the data shows as under-explored
- Which runtime constraints have been discovered and must be respected
- Whether L2 itself is the problem (validator failures on L2's output) and the plan must coach L2's next pass
l3_plan/1.answer_format:
Return a JSON object with:
  "plan": new strategy text for guiding future optimization (required)
  "note": OPTIONAL sticky pointer for the L2-layer (string or null). Persists across L2 fires until your next replan replaces it. Use it when the L2-layer keeps drifting away from a constraint your replan needs it to honor — e.g. a discovered runtime ceiling, a failed axis to avoid, or a specific cohort to focus on. Omit or null when the plan itself is enough.
  "rationale": 1-2 sentence explanation of the strategic shift

restructure/1.persona: You are a prompt engineering assistant.
restructure/1.task_intent: Your job is to structure user-provided context into Layer 1 prompt fields AND domain context fields for an optimization campaign.
restructure/1.instruction:
Layer 1 fields (for prompt construction):
- persona: Who the LLM should act as (e.g., 'You are a domain expert...')
- task_intent: What the prompt needs to accomplish
- problem_description: Description of the problem domain
- instruction: Core instruction text (may contain template variables)
- thinking_style: How to reason (e.g., 'Think step by step')
- answer_format: Expected output format

Domain context fields (for optimization guidance):
- domain: Research/industry domain (e.g., 'Life Cycle Assessment', 'Medical NLP')
- pipeline_purpose: What the pipeline does end-to-end in 1-2 sentences
- data_characteristics: What kind of data flows through (input format, volume, language)
- optimization_goals: What 'better' means in this context (accuracy metric, edge cases)
- key_challenges: Known difficulties, ambiguities, or edge cases the optimizer should know about
- upstream_context: What happens BEFORE this step — what data/processing feeds into it (e.g., 'Web search retrieves raw content from 7 pages'). Gets injected into the target prompt.
- downstream_context: What happens AFTER this step — how the output is consumed (e.g., 'Output fields are tokenized into words and matched against a database index by shared token count'). Gets injected into the target prompt.
restructure/1.thinking_style: Prefer the user's own wording for domain terms. Invent nothing — if a field has no source material, leave it sparse rather than padding it.
restructure/1.answer_format: Return a JSON object with Layer 1 fields at the top level AND a "task_context" key containing the domain context fields as a nested object. {{consultation_instruction}}
